title: LLMOps
scopeHtml: Scope: Observability, versioning, evals in CI, rollouts, feedback loops and drift.

notes.title: Observability
notes.html:
What to capture per request (trace).

  • Identifiers: trace id, user/tenant, session, feature, environment.
  • Versions: prompt version, model + snapshot id, parameters (temperature, max tokens), tool/schema versions, retrieval config, embedding model, guardrail policy version.
  • Inputs/outputs (with redaction): user message, rewritten query, retrieved chunk ids + scores, final prompt size, response, citations.
  • Execution: each model call and tool call as spans with latency, tokens (input/output/cached), cost, status, retries, finish reason.
  • Outcomes: user feedback, thumbs, edits, escalation, downstream success events.
  • Safety events: guardrail triggers, refusals, flagged content.

Metrics and dashboards.

  • Latency: TTFT, total, p50/p95/p99 per stage.
  • Throughput and queue depth; error rates by type (4xx, 429, 5xx, timeouts, validation failures).
  • Tokens and cost by feature/tenant/model; cache hit rates.
  • Quality proxies: groundedness/judge scores on sampled traffic, thumbs-up rate, escalation rate, retry/regeneration rate.
  • Safety: refusal rate, guardrail triggers, flagged outputs.
  • Retrieval: empty-result rate, average top score, recall probes.

Tooling. OpenTelemetry (GenAI semantic conventions), Langfuse, LangSmith, Arize Phoenix, Datadog/Grafana plus custom evaluators, provider consoles.

Privacy. Redact PII/secrets in traces, restrict access, set retention, support deletion; sample full prompts rather than storing everything when sensitive.

Alerting. SLO-based alerts (latency, error rate), cost anomaly alerts, quality drop alerts (judge score or thumbs-down spike), safety incident alerts.

Real life. The instrument panel and flight recorder of an airplane.

notes.title: Versioning everything
notes.html:
Versioned artifacts. Prompts and templates; model identifiers (pin dated snapshots, not floating aliases); sampling parameters; tool definitions and schemas; retrieval configuration (chunking, embedding model, index version, reranker); guardrail policies; evaluation datasets and graders; fine-tuned weights/adapters; application code.

Why. Any layer can change behaviour. Without versions you can't explain a regression, reproduce an answer, roll back precisely, or satisfy audits.

How.

  • Git for prompts/configs; or a prompt registry with immutable versions, labels (prod, staging), and change logs.
  • Attach a manifest (all versions) to each deployment and to each trace.
  • Immutable index versions with aliases; blue/green re-indexing.
  • Semantic versioning for schemas with backward-compatibility rules.
  • Dependency tracking (a schema change needs coordinated prompt, parser, consumer updates).
  • Reproducibility: record seeds where supported, but remember outputs may still vary.

Real life. Batch numbers on food products allow targeted recalls.

notes.title: Evals in CI/CD
notes.html:
Pipeline.

  1. Pre-commit/PR: fast checks: prompt lint, schema validation, unit tests for parsers/tools, small smoke eval (20 to 50 cases, cached where inputs unchanged).
  2. PR eval: golden set run for changes touching prompts/retrieval/models/tools; compare to baseline with confidence intervals; fail on regression beyond thresholds; post a report (score deltas by slice, new failures with examples).
  3. Nightly/weekly: full eval, adversarial/red-team suite, long-tail slices, cost/latency benchmarks, judge calibration drift check.
  4. Pre-release: shadow/canary stage with live metrics.
  5. Post-release: monitor online metrics and sampled auto-eval; feed failures into the dataset.

Practicalities. Control cost with sampling and caching of unchanged cases; pin the judge model; handle non-determinism with repeats; separate flaky tests; store results over time to chart trends; require human sign-off for safety-critical changes.

Real life. The assembly line's quality gate before shipping.

notes.title: Rollouts and experiments
notes.html:
Release strategies.

  • Feature flags for prompts/models/tools, per tenant or percentage.
  • Shadow: run new version in parallel, don't show output; compare.
  • Canary: 1 to 5% of traffic, auto-rollback on SLO/guardrail breaches.
  • A/B tests: randomize users, predefine primary metric and guardrails, adequate sample size and duration, analyze by segment.
  • Interleaving for ranking tasks.
  • Progressive delivery and kill switches.

Guardrail metrics. Latency, error rate, cost per request, safety violations, refusal rate, escalation rate, complaint rate.

Model upgrades. Treat as a release: eval on your suite, review diffs on failures, adjust prompts, shadow test, canary, keep rollback to the previous snapshot until stable.

Real life. Trying a new recipe at one branch before the whole chain.

notes.title: Feedback loops and data flywheel
notes.html:
Signals.

  • Explicit: thumbs up/down with reason, ratings, comments, "report" button, human corrections.
  • Implicit: regenerate, copy/paste, edits to the output, abandonment, follow-up reformulations, escalations to human, task completion events.
  • Expert review: sampled transcripts labelled by domain experts.
  • Automated evaluation on sampled traffic (judges, validators).

Loop. Collect → triage and cluster failures → root-cause (retrieval, prompt, tool, model, data) → fix → add as regression cases → evaluate → release → measure. Periodically use curated corrections as fine-tuning or few-shot data (with consent, privacy review and deduplication).

Pitfalls. Feedback bias (only extremes respond), feedback gaming, privacy/consent for reuse of user data, feedback loops reinforcing the model's own outputs (training on its output), noisy labels.

Real life. A restaurant reading comment cards every week and adjusting the menu.

notes.title: Drift and maintenance
notes.html:
Sources of drift.

  • Model drift: provider updates, deprecations, behaviour changes in unpinned aliases.
  • Data drift: new topics, products, languages in user queries; changing document corpus.
  • Concept drift: policies and definitions change (new refund policy).
  • Infrastructure drift: library upgrades, tokenizer or API changes.
  • Adversary drift: new jailbreak techniques.
  • Embedding/index drift: stale or mixed vectors.

Controls. Pin versions; scheduled eval runs on production samples; monitor distribution of queries (topic clustering, embedding drift), retrieval hit rates and judge scores over time; alert on shifts; periodic re-index and prompt review; deprecation calendar with migration drills; maintain an abstraction layer; regular red-team refresh.

Real life. Servicing a car on schedule, not only when it breaks.

notes.title: Reliability patterns
notes.html:
Failure types. Provider outage, rate limits (429), overload (5xx/529), timeouts, slow responses, malformed outputs, tool failures, retrieval failures, partial stream drops, quota exhaustion.

Patterns.

  • Timeouts on every external call, with budget propagation (deadline).
  • Retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors; honor retry-after; limit attempts; don't retry bad requests; avoid retry storms (retry budget, only one layer retries).
  • Circuit breakers to stop hammering failing dependencies.
  • Fallbacks: secondary model/provider, cached or simplified answer, non-AI path, queue for later.
  • Graceful degradation: disable optional features (reranking, long memory) under load; shed low-priority traffic.
  • Bulkheads: isolate pools per feature/tenant.
  • Idempotency for retried requests with side effects.
  • Health checks and load balancing; multi-region where required.
  • Chaos/fire drills: test failover regularly.
  • SLOs and error budgets to balance reliability with change velocity.

Real life. A backup generator and manual override for when the grid fails.

notes.title: Summary
notes.html:
Observability. Trace each request with all versions, prompts/outputs (redacted), retrieval ids/scores, model/tool spans, tokens, latency, cost, feedback and safety events; dashboards for latency percentiles, errors, cost, cache hits, quality proxies, retrieval health; SLO and anomaly alerts; privacy controls.

Versioning. Pin model snapshots; version prompts, tools, schemas, retrieval/index configs, guardrail policies and datasets; manifest per deployment and trace; immutable versions and aliases; precise rollback and audit.

CI/CD evals. Smoke on PR, golden set with thresholds on config changes, nightly full/adversarial suites, pre-release shadow/canary, post-release monitoring; control cost via sampling/caching; handle non-determinism.

Rollouts. Flags, shadow, canary, A/B with guardrail metrics, kill switches; model upgrades as full releases.

Feedback flywheel. Explicit + implicit + expert signals → triage → fix → regression cases → release; mind bias, consent and self-training loops.

Drift. Model, data, concept, infrastructure, adversary and embedding drift; pin, monitor, schedule re-evaluation and migrations.

Reliability. Timeouts, backoff with jitter and retry-after, single retry layer, circuit breakers, fallbacks, degradation, bulkheads, idempotency, drills, SLOs.

Interview one-liners.

  • "If you can't say which prompt and model version produced an answer, you can't operate the system."
  • "Pin model snapshots; upgrade like a release."
  • "Retries belong in one layer, with jitter and budgets."
  • "Production failures are the best eval cases you will ever get."
